internal_discovery.plain_explanation: In all three occurrences ص ر م sits inside one story (Sūrat al-Qalam 68:17-22, the garden owners). Two tokens are productive and agentive: the verb la-yaṣrimunna-hā (68:17, 'they swore they would surely ṣrm the garden at daybreak') and the active participle ṣārimīn (68:22, 'go early to your crop if you are ṣārimīn / reapers'), both bound to agricultural objects (the garden, the ḥarth). These fix the sense as 'cut the produce off the plant' = reap/strip. The third token is the noun ṣarīm (68:20, 'so by morning it became ka-l-ṣarīm'), where the garden is the patient after being struck by a ṭāʾif. Read as the resultative/patient face of the same nucleus ('a thing cut off / stripped bare') it completes an elegant agent-action-result irony, but it is a non-recurring nominal whose sense rests on narrative inference rather than internal triangulation, so the account is held at MODERATE and to this derivational family only.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: Does NOT mean 'destroy/ruin' — the destroying agent is a different lexical item (ṭāʾif, 68:19) and the human ṣrm they swore to was a benign self-interested harvest that never occurred. Does NOT mean generic 'gather/collect' without physical severance. Does NOT (on this evidence) extend to severing kinship, covenants, bonds, or any non-agricultural object — every datum is horticultural (jannah, ḥarth, fruit). Gives NO Quran-internal support for a temporal 'night/darkness' reading of ṣarīm (that gloss would be an imported lexical prior, excluded by source policy). The active participle ṣārimīn does NOT entail success — it is conditional (in kuntum) and the harvest never happens.
